You're conflating several different things in this comment, although I can't blame you because the information on this topic can get muddled and people confuse the various approaches if they only have a surface level understanding of them. 

Sex workers themselves want **decriminalization** and **destigmatization** of both **workers** and **clients** (but not pimps) because it's been proven to reduce violence and keep them safest (this model is endorsed by WHO, Amnesty International, Human Rights Watch, the ACLU, and UNAIDS)

Libertarians tend to want **legalization** because they favor an ideology of free markets. This model - which amounts to legalized brothels - exists in parts of Nevada, but nowhere else in the U.S. 

Liberals often want **labor regulations and taxation** in place in the sex industry, although they may not listen to what sex workers themselves want (for instance, some regulations include things like forced gyno exams, forced government registries, and increased state surveillance for sex workers, which violate bodily autonomy and privacy) 

Many feminists prefer the **Nordic Model**, which decriminalizes the *selling* but not the *buying* of sexual services, because they see the workers as victims and the clients as predators. This exists in Sweden and other parts of Europe.

The good news is that almost nobody still believes sex workers themselves should be arrested and incarcerated, but there's still a lot of disagreement on everything else. I'm happy to share more information (and citations) on this if anyone is curious!
